domain_label: Real-Time Render & Performance Envelope — Feasibility & Build-vs-Adopt
purpose: The feasibility layer for the water-drop drill's motion: keep every animation within a measured render-performance envelope on the target device — riding compositor-only transform/opacity, holding the ~16.7ms frame budget, using will-change sparingly, degrading gracefully so a slow device never janks the essential timer, treating haptics and audio as progressive enhancement no information depends on, and settling the hand-roll-vs-adopt-a-library question by benchmarking both prototypes rather than asserting — with every external number source-tagged given the build-env direct-fetch 403 blocks.
assumptions: no observed dataset, device benchmark, or profiling trace is supplied; all scores are heuristic priors and all device/library figures are UNKNOWN until measured
the web.dev, MDN, and csstools performance/API sources are snippet-grade (direct WebFetch to the canonical publishers 403-blocked in this build env) and are tagged for re-verification
the app ships React 18 / Vite, ts-fsrs, Recharts, and shadcn with NO animation/physics library, so build-vs-adopt is genuinely open [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §4/§5; APP_RECON §5]
exclusions: the aesthetic feel of the motion — curves, springs, choreography (developed in kb1)
the honesty/accessibility permission contract — reduced-motion, quantization, no-mastery, ESL floor, no-write (developed in kb2)
the actual engineering implementation, bundler config, and CI (owned by the build team)
the mechanic, encoding, item content, and copy (owned by engage, viz, qcraft, uxguide)
the specific numeric benchmark results, which are UNKNOWN until measured on the target device

glossary.definition: The per-frame time available to stay smooth — about 16.7 ms at 60 fps (1000/60); exceeding it causes perceptible jank [FACT-source: https://csstools.io/blog/css-animation-performance].

The browser's Layout -> Paint -> Composite stages; properties that trigger only Composite avoid main-thread layout and paint work [FACT-source: web.dev — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]].
transform, opacity, and (some) filter, which the browser can animate on the GPU/compositor thread without layout or paint [FACT-source: web.dev animations-guide — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]].

A CSS hint that promotes an element to its own compositor layer; used sparingly on actively-animating elements and cleared when idle, since over-use wastes memory [FACT-source: web.dev — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]].

navigator.vibrate(pattern) — mobile-only and heavily constrained (absent on iOS, removed in Firefox 129, a no-op on desktop, needs a user gesture and visible document, suppressible by DND) [FACT-source: MDN — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]].
A feedback layer (haptics, audio) that enriches feel where available but that no information depends on, so its absence changes nothing for the learner.

The discipline of deciding whether to hand-roll motion or adopt a library by prototyping both and benchmarking target-device frame time, never by assertion — mirroring viz's identical rule [FACT — viz.conflicts_and_dominance].
The browser API that runs a callback synced to the display refresh, the correct clock for hand-rolled physics, requiring batched reads/writes to avoid layout thrash.

A multi-point CSS timing function that samples a spring curve to approximate bounce without JavaScript, cheaper than a RAF spring but not interruptible [FACT-source: carmenansio — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]].
The graceful fallback full feel -> reduced polish -> static (reduced-motion) that drops polish before responsiveness or information so a slow device never janks the essential timer.

nodes.definition: Frame the feasibility layer: every feel graphux specifies (kb1) and permits (kb2) must run inside a MEASURED render-performance envelope on the target device. This KB defines the frame budget, the compositor-friendly property set, the feedback-channel constraints (haptics/audio), and the build-vs-adopt method — all as measured verdicts, never asserted numbers.

included: the render envelope as the feasibility gate on feel
measured verdicts over asserted numbers

pros.claim: Framing feel as bounded by a measured envelope stops beautiful motion that janks on the real device
pros.example: checking a proposed spring's cost against the frame budget before committing to it

cons.claim: The envelope can read as an engineering veto over design if not paired with a tuning method
cons.example: treating the budget as a blocker rather than a design constraint to optimise within

failure_modes: specifying feel with no regard for the render cost
asserting performance numbers the app cannot yet measure
acceptance_tests: the frame states the render envelope as the measured feasibility gate for all drill motion
revisit_triggers: a target-device benchmark revises the envelope

base.update_signal: a target-device benchmark revises the render envelope

nodes.definition: At 60 fps the browser has roughly 16.7 ms per frame (1000/60); miss it and users perceive jank [FACT-source: https://csstools.io/blog/css-animation-performance]. This is the hard number every drill animation is measured against on the target device. graphux states the budget but verifies device-specific headroom by measurement.

included: the ~16.7ms/frame budget at 60fps
jank as the cost of missing it

pros.claim: A concrete per-frame budget turns 'smooth' into a measurable target
pros.example: budgeting the fall+rise+splash to complete their per-frame work under 16.7ms

cons.claim: 60fps/16.7ms is a general target, not this device's measured headroom, which may be higher-refresh or slower
cons.example: assuming 16.7ms on a 120Hz device that actually has ~8.3ms, or a low-end device with less real headroom

failure_modes: treating 16.7ms as a device-verified headroom without measuring
designing to 60fps on a device with a different refresh rate
acceptance_tests: the ~16.7ms/frame budget is stated with the device headroom deferred to measurement
revisit_triggers: a device measurement revises the real per-frame headroom

base.update_signal: a device measurement revises the per-frame headroom

nodes.definition: The browser pixel pipeline is Layout -> Paint -> Composite; properties that trigger only the composite step avoid main-thread layout and paint work [FACT-source: https://web.dev/articles/animations-and-performance — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]. Understanding which stage a motion touches is the basis for keeping the drill within budget.

included: the Layout->Paint->Composite pipeline
which stage a motion triggers as the cost driver

pros.claim: Knowing the pipeline stages lets graphux predict a motion's cost before measuring it
pros.example: recognising that animating width forces layout+paint while transform does not

cons.claim: The pipeline description is snippet-grade here (direct fetch 403-blocked) and must be re-confirmed
cons.example: quoting the exact pipeline stages as FACT without the source-verify tag

failure_modes: ignoring which pipeline stage a motion triggers
assuming all CSS animation costs the same
acceptance_tests: the Layout->Paint->Composite pipeline is stated with the source tagged for verification
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the pipeline description

base.update_signal: a direct fetch revises the pixel-pipeline description

nodes.definition: transform, opacity, and (some) filter are compositor-only: they run on the GPU/compositor thread without main-thread layout or paint [FACT-source: https://web.dev/articles/animations-guide — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]. These are the properties the drill's fall, rise, squash/stretch, and splash should ride to stay within budget.

included: transform/opacity/(some)filter as compositor-only
the cheap property set for drill motion

pros.claim: Restricting drill motion to compositor-only properties gives the best chance of holding the frame budget
pros.example: fading the splash with opacity and moving the drop with transform, both compositor-only

cons.claim: The compositor-only claim is snippet-grade and browser-version-dependent; some filters still cost paint
cons.example: assuming every filter is free when some trigger paint on the main thread

failure_modes: animating expensive properties out of habit
assuming compositor-only behaviour without verifying per property
acceptance_tests: the drill motion is specified on transform/opacity/(compositor-safe)filter, with the source tagged
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the compositor-only property list

base.update_signal: a direct fetch revises the compositor-only property set

nodes.definition: Practical rules: animate translateX/Y not left/top, scale() not width/height, and fade with opacity — the left/top/width/height forms force layout every frame [FACT-source: https://web.dev/articles/animations-guide — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]]. A naive per-frame height/width tween of the water tank is the drill's main jank risk.

included: translate-not-left/top, scale-not-width/height, opacity-fade
the tank height/width tween as the jank risk

pros.claim: Concrete property rules make the cheap path unambiguous for the implementer
pros.example: implementing the water rise as a scaleY transform on a fixed-size element, not a height tween

cons.claim: A scale-based rise needs care so the water and its stepped scale stay pixel-crisp and correctly quantized
cons.example: a scaleY rise that blurs the step marks or misaligns the quantized levels

failure_modes: tweening height/width or left/top per frame
using scale in a way that distorts the quantized level marks
acceptance_tests: the rise/fall/splash use transform/opacity forms, and the tank is not animated via a height/width tween
revisit_triggers: a measurement shows the transform approach still janks and needs rework

base.update_signal: a measurement shows the transform approach still janks

nodes.definition: will-change hints the browser to promote an element to its own compositor layer, but over-use wastes memory and resources [FACT-source: https://web.dev/articles/animations-guide — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]]. graphux applies will-change only to the few elements that actually animate (drop, water, splash) and removes it when idle.

included: will-change only on the actively animating elements
removing it when idle to free resources

pros.claim: Sparing will-change gets the layer-promotion benefit without the memory cost of over-promotion
pros.example: promoting only the drop and water layers during the animation, then clearing will-change

cons.claim: Mis-timed will-change can hurt more than it helps, and its behaviour varies by browser
cons.example: leaving will-change on every element permanently and bloating memory

failure_modes: applying will-change to many static elements
never removing will-change after the animation ends
acceptance_tests: will-change is applied only to actively animating elements and cleared when idle, with the source tagged
revisit_triggers: a direct source check or measurement revises will-change guidance

base.update_signal: a direct fetch or measurement revises will-change guidance

nodes.definition: Consequence for the drill: the fall, rise, squash/stretch, and splash should ride transform/opacity so they run on the compositor; a naive per-frame height/width tween of the tank is a jank risk to be avoided [FACT-source: web.dev animations-guide — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]]. This node ties the general rules to each specific drill motion.

included: mapping fall/rise/squash/splash to transform/opacity
avoiding the tank height/width tween
excluded: the honesty of the scaled level (kb2)

pros.claim: Mapping each drill motion to a compositor property makes the implementation budget-aware by construction
pros.example: specifying the fall as translateY, the rise as scaleY, the squash as scale, the splash as opacity+scale

cons.claim: A scaleY rise must reconcile with kb2's quantization so the transform lands exactly on honest steps
cons.example: a scaleY value that lands between two floored steps and reads as a false continuum

failure_modes: implementing any drill motion via layout-triggering properties
letting a transform-based rise violate the quantization
acceptance_tests: each drill motion is mapped to a compositor property and reconciled with the quantized-step requirement
revisit_triggers: a measurement or kb2 quantization change forces a re-mapping

base.update_signal: a measurement or quantization change forces re-mapping the drill motions

nodes.definition: The Web Vibration API (navigator.vibrate(pattern)) is mobile-only and heavily constrained: Safari/iOS never shipped it, Firefox 129 removed it, desktop returns true but is a no-op, it requires a prior user gesture and a visible document, and DND/silent mode can suppress it [FACT-source: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Vibration_API — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked]]. Haptics is therefore unreliable across the drill's platforms.

included: navigator.vibrate mobile-only and its constraints
haptics as unreliable across platforms

pros.claim: Documenting the API's real limits stops the drill from depending on a feedback channel half its users lack
pros.example: noting iOS has no vibration at all before considering it for feedback

cons.claim: The specific version facts (Firefox 129 removal) are snippet-grade and must be re-verified
cons.example: quoting 'Firefox 129 removed it' as FACT without the source-verify tag

failure_modes: depending on vibration for feedback that some platforms cannot deliver
assuming desktop vibrate works because the call returns true
acceptance_tests: the Vibration API constraints are stated with the source tagged, establishing haptics as unreliable
revisit_triggers: a direct source check revises the Vibration API support facts

base.update_signal: a direct fetch revises the Vibration API support facts

nodes.definition: Because the Vibration API is absent on iOS, removed in Firefox 129, and a no-op on desktop, haptics is a PROGRESSIVE-ENHANCEMENT feedback layer only: never a channel any information depends on [FACT-source: MDN Vibration API — [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE]]. If haptics adds nothing beyond what the visual channel already conveys, its absence changes nothing.

included: haptics as pure progressive enhancement
no information depends on the haptic channel
excluded: the visual feedback that must duplicate it (kb1/kb2)

pros.claim: Treating haptics as enhancement-only keeps the drill fully functional where vibration is unavailable
pros.example: adding a subtle buzz on a hit as a bonus while the visual splash carries the actual confirmation

cons.claim: Enhancement-only haptics may feel underwhelming to users on devices where it does work well
cons.example: a strong-haptics Android user perceiving the drill as less tactile than a native game

failure_modes: making information depend on the haptic channel
adding haptics that duplicate no visual signal and thus mislead when absent
acceptance_tests: haptics is specified as progressive enhancement with a visual equivalent for every signal it carries
revisit_triggers: a decision to rely on haptics for any information is proposed

base.update_signal: a proposal would make information depend on haptics

nodes.definition: Audio feedback must likewise be optional and captioned by a visual equivalent: it may enrich the reward beat but cannot be the sole carrier of any information, since users may be muted, in silent mode, or hard-of-hearing. Every sound maps to a visual event that already conveys the same meaning.

included: audio as optional, always duplicated visually
no information carried by sound alone

pros.claim: Optional, visually-duplicated audio enriches feel without excluding muted or hard-of-hearing users
pros.example: a soft splash sound accompanying the visual splash, with the visual carrying the actual confirmation

cons.claim: Audio adds asset weight and autoplay-policy friction for marginal benefit in a study tool
cons.example: loading a sound pack that browsers may block from autoplaying without a gesture

failure_modes: making a sound the sole signal for an event
audio that plays without a visual equivalent
acceptance_tests: audio is optional and every sound has a visual equivalent that conveys the same meaning
revisit_triggers: a proposal would make information depend on audio

base.update_signal: a proposal would make information depend on audio

nodes.definition: The app ships NO animation/physics library today (React 18 / Vite, ts-fsrs, Recharts, shadcn) [FACT — GAMIFICATION_PLAN §4/§5; APP_RECON §5]. So whether to hand-roll motion or adopt a library is an open, unmeasured decision — graphux must not assert a library fact or performance number the app has never run.

included: the current stack has no animation/physics lib
build-vs-adopt is open and unmeasured

pros.claim: Recording that no motion lib exists forces every library/perf claim to be measured, not asserted
pros.example: refusing to state a spring library's frame cost because the app has never run it

cons.claim: The absence of a lib also means hand-rolled physics carries real implementation and correctness risk
cons.example: under-estimating the effort to hand-roll a stable spring loop from scratch

failure_modes: asserting a library's API or performance the app has never run
assuming hand-rolling is trivially cheaper without measuring
acceptance_tests: the no-animation-library fact is stated and every library/perf claim is gated on measurement
revisit_triggers: the app adopts an animation/physics library

base.update_signal: the app adopts an animation or physics library

nodes.definition: The hand-roll option: CSS transforms with the multi-point linear() timing function for spring-like easing, plus requestAnimationFrame for any physics that CSS cannot express. Cheap in dependencies, but the spring correctness and frame-budget discipline are graphux's to get right.

included: CSS transforms + linear() + requestAnimationFrame
zero-dependency but hand-owned correctness

pros.claim: Hand-rolling avoids a dependency and keeps full control of the compositor path and honesty constraints
pros.example: using CSS transitions with a linear() spring approximation for the water settle, no library added

cons.claim: Hand-rolled physics can be subtly wrong or costly, and re-implements what a mature library already solved
cons.example: a hand-rolled RAF spring that drifts or drops frames under load

failure_modes: hand-rolling complex physics that a library solves more reliably
a RAF loop that fights the compositor and janks
acceptance_tests: the hand-roll option is specified as CSS transforms + linear() + RAF with correctness and budget as graphux's responsibility
revisit_triggers: a benchmark shows hand-rolling misses the budget or is too error-prone

base.update_signal: a benchmark shows hand-rolling misses the budget

nodes.definition: The adopt option: bring in a spring/motion library that provides tested spring physics and a compositor-friendly animation runtime. Higher dependency and bundle cost, but proven physics and less hand-owned risk. Its actual API surface and performance are UNKNOWN until the specific library is prototyped in this app [UNKNOWN].

included: a spring/motion library for tested physics
bundle/dependency cost vs proven correctness

pros.claim: Adopting a proven library reduces physics-correctness risk and speeds spring/settle work
pros.example: using a maintained spring library's settle rather than hand-tuning damping from scratch

cons.claim: A library adds bundle weight and its real cost in THIS app is unknown until prototyped
cons.example: assuming a library's advertised performance holds in the app without measuring it

failure_modes: asserting an unprototyped library's performance as fact
adopting a heavy library for a single small drill
acceptance_tests: the adopt option is specified with its API/performance marked UNKNOWN-until-prototyped in this app
revisit_triggers: a specific library is prototyped and measured

base.update_signal: a specific library is prototyped and measured in the app

nodes.definition: The build-vs-adopt choice is a MEASURED verdict, never an asserted one — mirroring viz's identical discipline for graph-rendering libraries [FACT — viz.escalation + conflicts_and_dominance]. Method: prototype BOTH hand-rolled and adopted, measure frame time on the target device against the ~16.7ms budget, and decide by benchmark.

included: prototype-both, measure, decide by benchmark
a measured verdict, never asserted, mirroring viz

pros.claim: A prototype-and-measure method produces a defensible library decision grounded in the app's real numbers
pros.example: building a minimal hand-rolled and library prototype of the water settle and comparing measured frame time

cons.claim: Prototyping both costs time up front that a snap decision would skip
cons.example: the effort of two prototypes before committing to one path

failure_modes: asserting a build-vs-adopt verdict without prototyping both
deciding by reputation rather than target-device measurement
acceptance_tests: the build-vs-adopt decision is presented as a measured verdict from prototyping both against the frame budget
revisit_triggers: target-device benchmarks of both options are produced

base.update_signal: target-device benchmarks of both options are produced

nodes.definition: For any hand-rolled physics, requestAnimationFrame drives the loop synced to the display refresh; per-frame work must stay within the budget and reads/writes should be batched to avoid layout thrash. RAF is the correct clock for a hand-rolled fall/settle, but the loop must cooperate with, not fight, the compositor.

included: RAF as the refresh-synced clock for hand-rolled physics
per-frame budget and batched reads/writes

pros.claim: RAF gives frame-synced timing and a natural place to enforce the per-frame budget
pros.example: stepping a hand-rolled fall in a RAF callback that keeps its work under the frame budget

cons.claim: A poorly written RAF loop can thrash layout or run heavy work off the compositor and jank
cons.example: reading layout and writing styles interleaved each frame and forcing synchronous reflow

failure_modes: interleaving layout reads/writes in the RAF loop
doing heavy non-compositor work each frame
acceptance_tests: hand-rolled physics uses a RAF loop that batches reads/writes and holds the per-frame budget
revisit_triggers: a measurement shows the RAF loop thrashes layout or misses the budget

base.update_signal: a measurement shows the RAF loop misses the budget

nodes.definition: CSS's multi-point linear() timing function can approximate a spring by sampling its curve into many points, closing part of the gap between a bezier and a true spring without JavaScript [FACT-source: https://www.carmenansio.com/articles/spring-physics-css/ — snippet-grade]. This is the cheapest spring-like route for the water settle and splash recoil in the hand-roll option.

included: linear() as a JS-free spring approximation
the cheapest spring-like route for settle/recoil

pros.claim: A linear() spring approximation gives bouncy feel on the compositor with no JS loop and no library
pros.example: approximating the water settle with a multi-point linear() curve instead of a RAF spring

cons.claim: linear() only approximates a spring and cannot react to interruption like a real physics spring
cons.example: a linear() settle that cannot gracefully re-target mid-animation when a new hit lands

failure_modes: treating linear() as a full physics spring
using linear() where interruptible physics is actually needed
acceptance_tests: the water settle/recoil use a linear() approximation where a JS spring is not required, with the source tagged
revisit_triggers: a motion needs interruptible physics that linear() cannot provide

base.update_signal: a motion needs interruptible physics beyond linear()

nodes.definition: The envelope must hold with motion ENABLED (reduced-motion off is the heavier path), and the drill must degrade gracefully on a slow device — dropping polish before dropping responsiveness or information. graphux specifies a fallback ladder: full feel -> reduced polish -> static (reduced-motion) so a weak device never janks the essential timer.

included: holding the budget on the heavier motion-on path
a graceful degradation ladder for slow devices

pros.claim: A degradation ladder guarantees the essential timer stays smooth even when full polish cannot
pros.example: dropping the splash particles first on a slow device while keeping the fall and timer smooth

cons.claim: Defining device tiers risks asserting thresholds that are only knowable by measurement
cons.example: hardcoding a device-class cutoff without measuring where the budget actually breaks

failure_modes: janking the essential timer on a slow device to keep polish
asserting device-tier cutoffs without measurement
acceptance_tests: a degradation ladder (full feel -> reduced polish -> static) is specified with tier cutoffs deferred to measurement
revisit_triggers: device-tier measurements set the degradation cutoffs

base.update_signal: device-tier measurements set the degradation cutoffs

nodes.definition: Every external motion/performance/accessibility number in this envelope is snippet-grade because direct WebFetch to MDN, web.dev, and W3C 403'd in this build env; each such claim carries [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: direct-fetch 403-blocked] and routes to recon before it is asserted as law [FACT — build-env note]. graphux never upgrades a snippet to a fact silently.

nodes.definition: Synthesis: emit the feasibility verdict — the drill motion rides compositor-only properties, holds the ~16.7ms budget on the target device (measured), uses will-change sparingly, degrades gracefully, treats haptics/audio as progressive enhancement, and settles the build-vs-adopt question by benchmarking both prototypes. pros.claim: A single feasibility verdict makes the drill's motion shippable on the real device and honest about its numbers

conflict_axes.name: compositor_only_vs_expressive_properties
conflict_axes.description: Some expressive effects want properties (box-shadow, filter, layout) that trigger paint/layout and cost frames.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the frame budget dominates: prefer compositor-only transform/opacity and measure any paint-triggering effect before use

conflict_axes.name: hand_roll_control_vs_library_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Hand-rolling gives control and zero dependencies; a library gives tested physics but bundle cost.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: measurement dominates: prototype both and decide by target-device frame time, never by reputation

conflict_axes.name: rich_haptics_vs_cross_platform_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Haptics enriches feel but is absent on iOS, removed in Firefox 129, and a no-op on desktop.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: cross-platform reliability dominates: haptics is progressive enhancement and never carries information alone

conflict_axes.name: full_polish_vs_slow_device_smoothness
conflict_axes.description: Full polish is richer but can jank the essential timer on a weak device.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the essential timer dominates: drop polish before dropping responsiveness or information on a slow device

conflict_axes.name: asserted_perf_number_vs_measured_verdict
conflict_axes.description: Asserting a frame cost or device tier is faster than measuring it, but the app has never run this motion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: measured verdict dominates: device and library performance figures are benchmarked, never asserted

conflict_axes.name: snippet_source_vs_verified_fact
conflict_axes.description: A snippet-grade MDN/web.dev/W3C number is available now; a direct-fetch verification is not (403-blocked).
poles: tag it snippet-grade and route to recon
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: source discipline dominates: 403-blocked numbers stay tagged UNVERIFIED-SOURCE and route to recon before assertion

conflict_axes.name: aggressive_will_change_vs_memory_cost
conflict_axes.description: Promoting many layers with will-change can smooth animation but wastes memory.
poles: apply will-change sparingly and clear it
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sparing use dominates: will-change only on actively animating elements, removed when idle

conflict_axes.name: linear_approx_vs_true_interruptible_physics
conflict_axes.description: A CSS linear() spring is cheap but cannot re-target mid-animation like a real physics spring.
poles: use real physics where interruption matters
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fitness-for-purpose dominates: linear() where non-interruptible suffices, real/adopted physics where interruption is needed

conflict_axes.name: audio_richness_vs_accessibility_and_policy
conflict_axes.description: Audio enriches the reward beat but excludes muted/HoH users and hits autoplay policy.
poles: keep audio optional and visually duplicated
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: accessibility dominates: audio is optional and every sound has a visual equivalent

edge_cases.description: The water rise is implemented as a per-frame height tween of the tank and janks.
edge_cases.mitigation: re-implement the rise as a scaleY transform on a fixed-size element, reconciled with the quantized steps

edge_cases.description: A scaleY-based rise lands between two quantized steps and shows a false continuum.
edge_cases.mitigation: snap the transform to values that land exactly on viz's floored steps and damp overshoot

edge_cases.description: Haptic feedback is used to signal a correct hit and iOS users get nothing.
edge_cases.mitigation: duplicate the signal visually; haptics is enhancement only and iOS has no vibration

edge_cases.description: A build-vs-adopt decision is made from a library's advertised benchmarks, not the app's.
edge_cases.mitigation: prototype both in-app and decide by target-device frame time before committing

edge_cases.description: A RAF loop reads layout and writes styles interleaved each frame and forces reflow.
edge_cases.trigger: layout thrash in the RAF loop
edge_cases.mitigation: batch all reads then all writes and keep per-frame work under the budget

edge_cases.description: A snippet-grade web.dev compositor-property claim is asserted as law in the build spec.
edge_cases.mitigation: tag it UNVERIFIED-SOURCE and route to recon/a live check before it gates the build

edge_cases.description: Full polish janks the fall timer on a low-end phone.
edge_cases.trigger: slow device janks the essential timer
edge_cases.mitigation: engage the degradation ladder: drop splash particles first, keep the fall and timer smooth

edge_cases.description: will-change is left on every drill element permanently and memory balloons.
edge_cases.mitigation: apply will-change only during active animation and remove it when idle

edge_cases.description: A linear() settle cannot re-target when a new hit lands mid-animation and looks broken.
edge_cases.mitigation: use an interruptible RAF/library spring for that motion, or design the beat so interruption is not needed

edge_cases.description: A sound plays for an event with no visual equivalent and a muted user misses it.
edge_cases.mitigation: add a visual equivalent for the event; audio must never be the sole carrier

edge_cases.description: A 120Hz device is treated as having 16.7ms headroom when it actually has ~8.3ms.
edge_cases.mitigation: measure the actual refresh/headroom on the target device rather than assuming 60fps

edge_cases.description: The app adopts a motion library and old asserted hand-roll perf claims are now stale.
edge_cases.mitigation: re-run the benchmark under the new stack and update the measured verdict

workflow.description: State that all drill feel must run within a measured budget on the target device, with numbers deferred to measurement.
workflow.gate: the envelope is framed as the measured feasibility gate before any perf claim

workflow.action: Fix the frame budget and pipeline
workflow.description: State the ~16.7ms/frame budget and the Layout->Paint->Composite pipeline, with device headroom deferred to measurement.
workflow.gate: the budget and pipeline are stated with sources tagged

workflow.action: Map each drill motion to a compositor property
workflow.description: Assign fall/rise/squash/splash to transform/opacity, avoid height/width tweens, and reconcile with the quantized steps.
workflow.gate: every motion rides a compositor property and respects quantization

workflow.action: Constrain haptics and audio to enhancement
workflow.description: Specify haptics and audio as optional, visually-duplicated channels no information depends on.
workflow.gate: no information depends on haptics or audio

workflow.description: State that the app has no motion library and lay out the hand-roll and adopt options without asserting perf.
workflow.gate: both options are stated with library/perf claims gated on measurement

workflow.description: Define the CSS transform + linear() + RAF hand-roll path and where linear() vs interruptible physics applies.
workflow.gate: the hand-roll path is specified with its limits noted

workflow.description: Prototype both, measure target-device frame time against the budget, and decide by benchmark.
workflow.gate: the decision is a benchmark, not an assertion

workflow.description: Define full feel -> reduced polish -> static so a slow device never janks the essential timer.
workflow.gate: the essential timer stays smooth on a weak device

workflow.description: Mark every 403-blocked MDN/web.dev/W3C claim UNVERIFIED-SOURCE and route it to recon before assertion.
workflow.gate: no snippet-grade number is asserted as law

workflow.description: Assemble the compositor/budget/degradation/haptics/build-vs-adopt verdict with every number source-tagged and measured.
workflow.gate: every device/library figure is a measured, source-tagged verdict

dominance_rules.rule: The frame budget dominates expressive property choice
dominance_rules.rationale: paint/layout-triggering effects miss the budget and jank
dominance_rules.trigger: a motion wants a paint/layout-triggering property
dominance_rules.action: prefer compositor-only transform/opacity; measure any exception

dominance_rules.rationale: the app has never run this motion, so any perf number is a guess
dominance_rules.trigger: a device or library perf figure is needed
dominance_rules.action: benchmark it on the target device; never assert it

dominance_rules.rule: The essential timer dominates full polish
dominance_rules.rationale: a janky timer breaks the drill's core function
dominance_rules.trigger: a slow device cannot render full polish
dominance_rules.action: degrade polish first; keep the timer and responsiveness smooth

dominance_rules.rationale: half the drill's platforms cannot deliver vibration
dominance_rules.action: treat it as progressive enhancement with a visual equivalent

dominance_rules.rationale: muted/HoH users and autoplay policy exclude sound-only signals
dominance_rules.trigger: a sound would carry a signal
dominance_rules.action: make audio optional and duplicate it visually

dominance_rules.rationale: an unverified number gives false engineering assurance
dominance_rules.trigger: a 403-blocked source is needed as a fact
dominance_rules.action: tag UNVERIFIED-SOURCE and route to recon before asserting

dominance_rules.rule: Prototype-both dominates a snap library decision
dominance_rules.rationale: a reputation-based choice may miss the app's real cost
dominance_rules.action: prototype hand-rolled and adopted and measure both

dominance_rules.rationale: linear() cannot re-target mid-animation like real physics
dominance_rules.action: use RAF/library physics there; linear() only where non-interruptible suffices

dominance_rules.rationale: over-promotion wastes memory and can regress performance
dominance_rules.action: limit it to actively animating elements and clear it when idle

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map drill motions to compositor properties before implementing them
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-writing a height/width tween that janked after shipping

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile transform-based rises with the quantized steps up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-doing a scaleY rise that showed a false continuum

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat haptics/audio as enhancement from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: stripping an information-bearing haptic after iOS users report missing feedback

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prototype both build and adopt before choosing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-implementing on the other path after an asserted verdict proved wrong on device

anti_rework_rules.rule: Batch reads/writes in any RAF loop from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: un-thrashing a layout-thrashing loop discovered in profiling

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every 403-blocked source at authoring time
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-auditing the spec for snippet-grade numbers asserted as law

anti_rework_rules.rule: Specify the degradation ladder before device testing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retrofitting graceful degradation after a slow device janked the timer

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear will-change when idle by design
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hunting a memory regression from permanently-promoted layers

iteration_protocol.trigger: a direct fetch confirms or revises the web.dev pixel-pipeline / compositor-only list, the csstools frame-budget figure, and the MDN Vibration API facts (snippet-grade / 403-blocked here)
iteration_protocol.action: replace UNVERIFIED-SOURCE tags with cited FACTs and re-check any rule that leaned on a revised claim

iteration_protocol.trigger: target-device benchmarks of the hand-rolled and adopted prototypes are produced
iteration_protocol.action: settle the build-vs-adopt verdict on the measured numbers and update the feasibility verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: the app adopts an animation/physics library
iteration_protocol.action: re-frame the no-library assumption and re-run the benchmark under the new stack
set the degradation-ladder cutoffs from the measured tiers

iteration_protocol.trigger: kb2's quantization changes the step model
iteration_protocol.action: re-map the transform-based rise to land on the new steps

iteration_protocol.trigger: a motion is found to need interruptible physics linear() cannot provide
iteration_protocol.action: move that motion to a RAF/library spring and re-measure

priority_rationale: The envelope frame, frame budget, and pixel pipeline come first because they define the measured gate; the compositor mapping, haptics/audio constraints, and hand-roll/adopt options operationalise it; the measured build-vs-adopt verdict, degradation ladder, source discipline, and feasibility verdict close the layer so every device/library number is measured and tagged, never asserted.
